after: Their name is heard beside the Quran’s image of return and re-creation.
reason: The dictionary separates the tribe name from the return sense, so this is an echo, not a translation of عَادًا. The verb يُعِيدُهُۥ in 29:19 calls that return sense; beside the visible remains of ʿAd, it lets the warning about a ruined people open onto the surah’s theme of creation returning.

after: The abandoned dwellings become the evidence through which clarity emerges.
reason: B004 describes something coming out of obscurity into view. The phrase مِن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ makes the dwellings the source of what has become clear, so the ruins themselves carry the disclosure.

after: The dwelling image holds the stillness left after the people’s movement ends.
reason: The focus names the places where the people lived, while B001 names motion coming to rest. The preceding account says they became جَٰثِمِينَ in their home; that stillness activates the root’s quieter image inside the surviving dwellings.

before: He beautified their deeds for them.
after: Beautification becomes a worked-over appearance competing with their capacity to discern.
reason: B002 is the act of making beauty appear, by action or speech. The closing مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ names people equipped with insight, so their perceptiveness sharpens the irony: attractive presentation led them away despite their capacity to see.

after: The distant one makes distance from the path happen to others.
reason: B001 carries the image of being far off or making someone distant. Here عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ supplies the separation and route: the following diversion makes the remoteness in the adversary’s name an enacted distance from guidance.

after: Their beautified works are shadowed as a well-worn track leading away.
reason: The ordinary sense is their deeds, but B011 preserves a rare work-root branch for a traveled, well-trodden road. The next phrase, ٱلسَّبِيلِ, supplies that route image, so the works they have been taught to admire can also be heard as a track carrying them from the way.

after: The diversion takes on the image of a barrier set across a route.
reason: The focus says فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ, naming both obstruction and its path-shaped target. B005 records a mountain or mountain face that blocks passage; the word for the way calls that barrier image even though no mountain is named.

after: Alongside the road sense, the word carries the image of rain descending and reviving the earth.
reason: B005 gives سبل the sense of rain falling between cloud and ground. Later the surah describes water sent down from the sky that brings the earth back to life, calling that rain image beside the path from which these peoples were turned.

after: Their claimed perceptiveness is measured against a sign made clear to its beholders.
reason: B003 describes an illuminating sign that makes people able to perceive. The neighboring town’s remains are called ءَايَةًۢ بَيِّنَةًۭ in 29:35, so the surah sets perceptive people beside evidence that has been made plain.

after: The named people become one counted case in a catalogue of distinct outcomes.
reason: This echo-root candidate does not make عَادًا mean “counted”; the name remains a proper name. But B001’s counting sense is called by فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا, which gathers the named communities into a reckoning where each is taken according to its offense.

before: The path from which they were turned.
after: The warning answers the Fatiha’s recurring plea for guidance along the straight path.
reason: B001 includes a road or way that brings one toward an end, including the religious path in the appropriate phrase. The Fatiha asks ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ, making the old diversion a warning heard alongside a continually recited request for guidance.

before: The dwellings left by the named peoples.
after: The surviving homes become a measure of whether a dwelling can truly shelter its inhabitants.
reason: B002 names the place where people settle and live. The surah later calls the spider’s house the weakest of houses; beside the dwellings that remain as evidence in 29:38, that fragile refuge makes habitation itself a test of protection.
